criteria.text: The workbook is saved under ./out/ with a .xlsx extension (./out/<name>.xlsx), and the ./out/ directory is created if it is missing (for example os.makedirs with exist_ok).
The final message states the relative path of the produced .xlsx file so the orchestration layer can collect it.
The workbook is built by writing a Python script that uses openpyxl and running it through Bash. It is not built by calling mcp__office__excel_* tools during a headless run.
criteria.source: How to build the workbook / When NOT to use

criteria.text: Hardcoded input values sit on a dedicated Inputs sheet. Calculation cells on other sheets are Excel formulas (strings starting with '=') that reference those inputs, not literal numbers.
criteria.source: Conventions: No hardcodes in calc cells

criteria.text: Font colors follow the blue/black/green convention: hardcoded inputs are blue (e.g. 0000FF), formulas are black, and cross-sheet or cross-file links are green.
The workbook includes a Checks sheet with formulas that test model integrity (for example, balance sheet balances or cash flow ties to cash) and evaluate to TRUE/FALSE.
Values meant to be referenced from a deck or memo, such as key outputs, are defined as named ranges in the workbook.
The response creates a new standalone workbook holding one model. It does not open and append to an existing workbook unless the user explicitly asked for that.
The workbook's formulas and labels correctly carry out the specific model or analysis the user requested, such as the right line items and correct calculation logic between cells.
criteria.source: Skill purpose: deliver an Excel workbook as a file artifact
